questions.q: What entry condition does the New Lead Auto-Assignment Flow use?
options: Lead Source equals Trade Show
None -- it runs for every newly created Lead, regardless of source
Estimated Locations is greater than 10
Owner is blank
questions.explain: The Flow has no entry filter, since Jordan Kessler owns every new Lead regardless of which of the four lead sources it came from.

questions.q: Besides setting the Lead's Owner, what else does Flow 1 do?
options: Sends an email to Monica Reyes
Converts the Lead automatically
Creates a follow-up Task assigned to Jordan Kessler, due the next day
Deletes any duplicate Lead records
questions.explain: A second action on the same Flow creates a Task -- "Qualify new lead" -- so Jordan has a same-day follow-up reminder instead of just an ownership change.

questions.q: What input variable does the Screen Flow in this lesson rely on to know which Installation Project to update?
options: A hardcoded record ID
recordId, passed in from the record the user launched the Flow from
The logged-in user's role
The Opportunity's Stage field
questions.explain: The Screen Flow uses a recordId input variable and a Get Records element to load the specific Installation Project the installer launched it from.

questions.q: Why is the service-visit Screen Flow launched as a Quick Action on the Installation Project layout instead of asking installers to use the standard Edit screen?
options: The standard Edit screen doesn't exist on custom objects
Quick Actions are required for all Screen Flows
It gives installers a fast, focused way to log a visit from the field without exposing the full record edit layout or fields outside their job
It's the only way to update a picklist field in Salesforce
questions.explain: The lesson frames this as a usability and scope choice -- a guided, two-screen flow for a specific field task, instead of the full edit layout.

questions.q: Which two record-triggered Flow timing options does Flow 1 use, and why?
options: Before save, because it only updates fields on the triggering record itself
After save, because it both updates the record and creates a related Task, which requires the record to already exist
Scheduled, running once per day on all Leads
Platform event-triggered, firing from an external system
questions.explain: Creating a related Task that references the Lead requires the Lead to already be saved, so the Flow runs after save rather than as a faster before-save update.
